title: Marginalia: Notes on Long-Window Benchmarks, Retrieval Latency, and Eval Hygiene
content:
Quick personal marginalia from reading papers and watching a few conference talks (NeurIPS/MLSys recaps) about long-context evaluation, retrieval-in-the-loop latency effects, and practical eval hygiene. Mostly shorthand, open questions, and things to try on Redwood eval infra.

1) High-level takeaways
- Long-context benchmarks are converging on two failure modes: hallucination drift over window and context-sensitivity (answers depend on exact placement of prompt snippets).
- Retrieval/RAG papers often report quality gains but bury the latency/cost tradeoff; real infra needs precise SLO-aware routing (send to cached variant vs fresh retrieval).
- Eval hygiene matters: many published gains are brittle to prompt formatting, truncation, and subtle pre-tokenization differences.

2) Papers/notes to re-check (links below)
- "Windowed Attention Distillation" (paper X) — interesting: distill model to approximate full attention for specific long-window distributions. Pro: cheaper KV usage. Con: brittle to sequence-length mismatch.
- "Latency-aware Retrieval for Online Systems" (demo) — key idea: quantify tail latency contribution per retrieved doc and include as routing feature. Could be folded into Redwood routing policies.
- "Prompt Insertion Order Effects" (short workshop paper) — simple but alarming experiments: permutation of facts in context changes scoring by nontrivial amounts.

3) Concrete experiments to run on Redwood eval harness
- Controlled placement test: take a gold fact, place at varying offsets from 0 to 32k tokens, measure answer correctness decay curve across models and quantizations. Use both hosted variants and dedicated low-quantization variants to see if quantization exacerbates drift.
- Retrieval latency SLO sim: synthetic workloads where retrieval cost is variable (fast cache hit vs slow cold repo), measure end-to-end tail latency and how different routing policies impact cost and error. Instrument with token-level cost breakdowns (Console traces).
- Prompt-format robustness sweep: tokenize + detokenize variants, whitespace/no-newline, and subtle punctuation changes. Compare outputs using string overlap vs semantic embedding similarity to detect near-miss answers.

4) Questions / hypotheses
- Hypothesis: KV compression and quantization interact nonlinearly with long-window degradation; at some point cheap KV causes more rerolls/fallbacks which offset cost savings. Need cost-quality curve.
- Question: can we use a lightweight verifier model (tiny classifier) to decide when to request retrieval vs rely on cached prefixes? Tradeoff: verifier cost vs avoided retrieval cost.
- Operational question: how often do prompt-formatting bugs explain "regressions" in production evals vs model updates? Need better diffing tool that highlights tokenization-sensitive diffs.

5) Implementation notes / TODOs
- Write a small Redwood eval driver that: 1) inserts a fact at parametric offsets, 2) records tokenization boundaries and final token counts, 3) stores answer embeddings for semantic comparison. Tie outputs to existing traces so we can correlate cost.
- Add a new trace tag: "placement-offset-N" so Console can aggregate latency/cost by offset buckets.
- Prototype a verifier: 100–200M classifier on sentence embedding, trained on tiny synthetic dataset of correct/incorrect answers. Keep it behind a routing policy.

6) Rough timeline (personal sprint)
- Week 1: quick placement sweep on 2 models (hosted baseline + dedicated int8). Gather curves.
- Week 2: implement retrieval-latency SLO sim and basic routing policy experiment (cache-first vs retrieval-first).
- Week 3: prompt-format robustness sweep + build diffing helper.

7) Quick links & artifacts
- saved-run: eval/placement-sweep/2029-09-30 (local eval id)
- draft slack note to eng-serve: "placement-offset anomalies" (will iterate)

Open thoughts (brain-dump):
- Could use adaptive chunking: if answer seems short/high-confidence, only prime first K tokens of context. Need to measure error envelope.
- For Dedicated customers with strict cost budgets, offer an "offset SLA" where we characterize performance by effective context window rather than raw tokens. Could be a differentiator.
- Eval hygiene: add a preflight check that runs 10 small perturbations of each eval prompt and flags items with >X variability; treat those as unstable and exclude from key metrics.

Unresolved bits I want to ask _Research_ and _Serving Runtime_:
- Research: any prior internal runs on verifier classifier?
- Runtime: feasibility of tagging traces with custom experiment metadata at ingest time without blowing up trace ingestion.

Notes-to-self end.
